newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS -Funding fears loom over rupiah,baht.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS -Funding fears loom over rupiah,baht.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah held steady on Tuesday with activity largely confined to players extending their forward positions while unloading some long dollar exposures.
Jakarta dealers said offshore dollar sales were countered by domestic demand for the U.S. unit due to ample money market liquidity and continued wariness of post-election unrest.
"There is no initiative to create fresh positions. We see mainly roll-over trades," a major local bank dealer said.

He said offshore operators appeared to extend long forward positions on fears the central bank might follow measures taken by the central Bank of Thailand (BOT) to stop local banks quoting tom/next swaps to offshore parties.
Bank Indonesia officials have denied any such plans.
But offshore players were still holding on to long forward positions despite suffering losses on the recent cheap short-term swap rates, the dealer said.
"They seem to take on such a calculated cost rather then being squeezed unexpectedly," he added.
Spot rupiah was at 2,429.5/30.0 at 0430 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/30.0.
Dealers said election issues continued to hang over the market as the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) is due to decide on Thursday whether to accept the election outcome.
PPP had alleged widespread election irregularities.
The ruling Golkar swept more than 74 percent of the votes counted, with the PPP taking nearly 23 percent.

The Thai baht eased but dealers said activity in offshore markets continued to be dominated by players selling dollars to cover their short baht positions as the central bank's ban on offshore lending of baht remained in place.
"There's selling interest from a U.S. fund around 24.85/90 but not much business other than that," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.

The baht was quoted at 24.700/24.800 to the dollar at 0430 GMT in offshore markets against 24.750/24.850 late on Monday. In the onshore market, the baht was traded at 25.860/25.875 compared with 25.820/25.850 late on Monday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.84 per dollar versus 25.81 on Monday.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was traded at 120/150 satangs per dollar offshore compared with 20/30 satangs onshore.

"There's a lot of long dollar positions on the outright that are maturing into mid-June. People have to either roll them over in the forward market, which is very expensive, or they have to sell dollars to get back baht," the Singapore dealer said.
But he said the volumes going through were likely to be small as there had been practically no interbank market for the baht since the BOT's restrictions were imposed.
"Most of the business is going through the brokers and their prices are only good for three (million) dollars, five (million) dollars," he said.
In Malaysia, the ringgit remained weak after coming under early pressure from strength in the dollar/majors and some selling of the ringgit against the Singapore dollar.
But demand for the ringgit out of Kuala Lumpur and fears of central bank intervention would limit its downside to about 2.5190/5200 for the time being, dealers said.
The Singapore dollar recovered from its lows as early buying of the ringgit/Sing cross in Sydney switched course.
"The ringgit/Sing had difficulty going above the 0.5700 level so the sellers came back in," a dealer said, adding that the cross was likely to trade a 0.5680-0.5705 range.
It was quoted at 0.5689/93 at 0430 GMT while the Singapore dollar was at 1.4319/24 against its U.S. counterpart.
-- Syed Azman in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
